deadlock commonly refers.high: Deadlock commonly refers to a situation where two or more processes are each waiting for the other to take action. The main detail is that the system keeps things predictable.
deadlock commonly refers.mid: A deadlock is when processes wait for each other, but all requests are granted immediately and no cycle is ever checked.

mutual exclusion.high: A single process at most can hold a resource.
mutual exclusion.mid: Only one process may hold a resource at a time, but all processes can use it together.

hold and wait.high: A process holds on to resources while asking for more.
hold and wait.mid: A process holds resources while requesting more, but it must release all held resources before asking and cannot keep any.

no preemption.high: A resource cannot be forcibly taken.
no preemption.mid: A resource cannot be forcibly taken, but resources are released automatically when another process asks.

circular wait.high: Processes form a cycle, each waiting for another.
circular wait.mid: There is a cycle of processes each waiting for the next, but it is not a cycle in practice.

resource allocation graph.high: It is a directed graph of allocations.
resource allocation graph.mid: It is a directed graph of process allocations, but it records only process names.

safe state.mid: Every process can finish in some order, but no process may ever request another resource because all resources are assigned to one process.

deadlock detection.high: The system checks the graph for a deadlock cycle periodically.
deadlock detection.mid: The system checks the graph for a deadlock cycle periodically, but it checks CPU temperature once per second.

recovery by rollback.high: Recovery rolls back to break the deadlock.
recovery by rollback.mid: A process is rolled back to break the deadlock, but it restarts the entire machine.

atomicity.high: A transaction is all-or-nothing: either every operation commits completely or none of them do.
atomicity.mid: A transaction is all-or-nothing, but transactions are split into smaller updates that each commit separately.

consistency.mid: A committed transaction preserves invariants, but it may violate rules.

isolation.high: Partial work is hidden from other transactions.
isolation.mid: Concurrent transactions cannot see partial effects, but they read uncommitted writes.

durability.mid: Committed changes survive a crash, but it requires the database to shut down after every commit.

two-phase locking.high: Locks grow during one phase then shrink during a later phase.
two-phase locking.mid: Locks grow then shrink, but it alternates acquiring and releasing every second.

write-ahead logging.high: The log is written before data pages are stored on disk.
write-ahead logging.mid: The log is written before data pages, but the log is kept in memory and never flushed to disk.

serializability.high: A concurrent schedule matches a serial order.
serializability.mid: The schedule matches a serial order, but all transactions use the same table.

savepoint.high: It is a point in a transaction that lets you roll back.
savepoint.mid: This point lets you roll back part of a transaction, but it is a backup of the whole database stored offsite.

fcfs.high: Processes are served in arrival order.
fcfs.mid: Processes are served in arrival order, but it gives each process a fixed time slice.

sjf.mid: The shortest job runs first, but the process that waited the longest runs.

round robin.high: Processes take turns with a fixed slice.
round robin.mid: Processes take turns with a fixed slice of CPU time in a cyclic queue, but it selects only the shortest burst each time.

time quantum.high: It is a fixed CPU slice before moving to the next.
time quantum.mid: It is the fixed maximum CPU time slice in one turn before being switched, but it is the amount of memory reserved.

preemption.high: The scheduler can interrupt a running process.
preemption.mid: The scheduler can interrupt a running process, but it increases the priority of long-waiting jobs.

starvation.high: A job can wait forever because other jobs are chosen.
starvation.mid: A process can wait forever because other jobs are chosen, but starvation ends a process immediately.

aging.high: Long-waiting processes are promoted step by step.
aging.mid: Long-waiting processes are promoted, but it assigns priorities randomly.

turnaround time.mid: It is the total time from submission to completion, but it is the length of one time quantum.
